doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Yale archive, video interviews and closing
summary: Talk of the Stanley Dance archive at Yale, the value of video, and thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well this has really been fascinating.

It’s interesting to talk with you. And I think it’s wonderful what you’re doing, doing this archive. I was in close touch with Harold Samuels, who’s the librarian at Yale, and who’s the man that originally was very impressed with everything Stanley had done, and called Stan and said what about this, and then what about the photographs, and then finally, what about the records, and of course it’s a big archive. And it was really a big step for us too because you know it’s hard to make a living in this world, in this music world. And it was a big step, so I think it was important. So I know about the situation about the archives and you’re doing just the same thing.
I think our strength in our archive will be the video interviews. Some other archives have interviews, they’re mostly audio. I think it’s important to see the person.
I do too. You’ve got that which Yale doesn’t. They don’t have that.
And as I said to Stanley, we will be collecting and acquiring other material to accompany the archive.
I had something very interesting that I brought for you to see. Stanley thinks that you will want to see it, so after I’ll show it to you.
Well on behalf of Hamilton I’d like to thank you for your time today, and it’s been a pleasure all the way around.
It was a pleasure. It’s always a nice world to talk about you know.
